_meta.purpose: Canonical AWS-service -> GCP-service classification (the 'logical construct'). Single source of truth used by service_classifier.py to force the correct GCP target and eliminate LLM label variance. Grounded in Google's official 'Google Cloud for AWS professionals' service comparison. Curate this file to add/adjust services.

mode_semantics.keep: Pipeline already prices this well deterministically — classifier only STAMPS metadata (category/reason), never changes pricing or the mapped SKU.
mode_semantics.review: Correct GCP target is known but precise GCP pricing needs per-service modelling. Classifier FORCES gcp_service=target + strategy=passthrough (carry AWS cost, no invented figure) + manual-review flag. Honest baseline until a deterministic pricer is built.
mode_semantics.ignore: Not a real workload cost on GCP (burstable CPU credits, billing fees, taxes, support, refunds). Classifier FORCES strategy='ignore' -> $0. GCP has no equivalent charge.

_meta.match: Case-insensitive substring against the AWS product name with the leading 'Amazon '/'AWS ' stripped. First match wins, so order specific -> general.
_meta.field_order_note: Downstream row metadata stored as: category, gcp_service, confidence, rule='service_map_v1', reason (in projection_note).

rules.reason: CloudTrail charges per recorded management/data event; Cloud Logging charges primarily by ingested log volume — a direct event-count-to-log-volume conversion has no reliable basis without knowing average event size, retention, exclusions, and sink configuration. A prior version priced this directly via an LLM event-to-GB guess (confirmed real: one job showed a 97.5% 'saving' the report's own outlier detection flagged as suspicious). Passthrough at AWS cost until a real CloudTrail-specific sizing model exists; architecture review recommended.
Multi-component (metrics + logs + alarms + dashboards). Single-SKU mapping under-projected badly (~0.07x); passthrough baseline until component pricer built.

NOTE: mode changed review->keep — apply_static_mappings.py handles both the Hours row (via FLAT_HOURLY_MAP Private Nat Gateway Uptime) and the Bytes row (via map_data_transfer NatGateway-Bytes branch); review mode was forcing passthrough unconditionally before either pricer ran, losing ~20% savings on NAT-heavy bills.

EKS cluster management fee ($0.10/hr/cluster) -> GKE Standard cluster fee ($0.10/hr). Underlying EC2 node costs appear as separate EC2 line items. NOTE: match text was 'elastic kubernetes' before, which never matches AWS's real EKS product string ('Amazon Elastic Container Service for Kubernetes') at all — it's the marketing name (EKS), not the CUR billing product name. That gap let the ECS/Fargate rule below (a genuine substring match on 'elastic container service') incorrectly catch every real EKS row instead, stamping an ECS-Fargate-flavored note ('ECS on EC2 nodes are billed as EC2...') on rows that are actually EKS control-plane fees. Fixed the match text to the real product string, and changed mode review->keep since map_flat_hourly already resolves a real, deterministic 'Zonal Kubernetes Clusters' SKU for these rows — review mode would have unconditionally clobbered that with a generic passthrough, same clobbering-bug class already fixed for ElastiCache/EFS/EMR/etc. elsewhere in this file.
ECS Fargate tasks -> GKE Autopilot pod capacity. ECS on EC2 nodes are billed as EC2 — those appear as separate EC2 line items.
Fargate vCPU/memory hours -> GKE Autopilot pod CPU/memory resources (directional estimate).

FaaS -> Cloud Run Functions (per invocation + GB-second memory). NOTE: mode changed review->keep — 'review' mode was unconditionally overwriting a real SKU/rate with a generic passthrough before this rule ever ran (same clobbering pattern found and fixed for ElastiCache/EFS/Public-IPv4). CORRECTION: for CUR-format bills (pricing_unit='Requests'/'Lambda-GB-Second'), map_per_request() in apply_static_mappings.py resolves this deterministically against the real 'Cloud Run Functions' service (previously mis-targeted at the sibling 'Cloud Run' service, which has no Lambda-relevant SKUs at all — fixed). For PDF-format bills where pricing_unit doesn't match those tokens, the row falls to mechanic_group='misc' and is resolved by the Phase 2 LLM via find-sku.sh instead — not deterministic, may vary run to run. keep only stamps category/confidence either way.

'keep' only stamps category/confidence, never touches strategy/gcp_service/gcp_sku_id.
